title: runtime-aware publish contract with sampled cost signatures
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Define and ship a lightweight, runtime-aware performance profile publish contract that includes sampled-inference cost signatures and validation hooks for pinning. Goal: enable automated publish of Redwood-verified profiles that reflect both synthetic benchmark signatures and sampled live-costs under representative runtime settings, while keeping the publish artifact small and human-reviewable.
background: We currently publish verified performance profiles based primarily on offline benchmarks (latency p50/p95, throughput, quantized cost estimates). Customers and infra teams have requested profiles that better reflect real serving conditions (batching patterns, KV cache hit rates, kernel variants) because offline numbers diverge from production costs by up to 20-30% for some workloads. This ticket formalizes a publish contract that combines canonical synthetic signatures with a sampled live-cost signature and explicit runtime constraints for pinning decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A publish contract document exists describing required fields for a Redwood-verified profile: model_version, synthetic_signatures, sampled_cost_signature, runtime_constraints, recommended_pin_policy, provenance_metadata
CI validation checks added: schema lint, synthetic benchmark ingest, sampled-cost rollup verification
Console UI shows sampled-cost delta against synthetic baseline on the profile page
Automated pin suggestion engine uses sampled-cost-adjusted cost metric when recommending pin targets
Playbook for canary publish and rollback documented and an initial internal canary completed
tasks: Draft publish contract spec and example JSON artifact (PM lead)
Add schema validator to profiles repo (Eng: data and runtime teams)
Instrument sampled-cost pipeline: sample 1% of live inference traffic for cost telemetry and aggregate into per-model signatures (Infra)
Update profile ingestion pipeline to accept sampled_cost_signature and runtime_constraints (Eng)
Console: add sampled cost visualization and guidance text (Console UI)
Pinning service: incorporate sampled-cost adjustment in recommendation algorithm (Platform)
Run internal canary: pick two non-critical models and publish runtime-aware profiles, compare behavior for 48 hours (PM/SE)
Create rollback playbook and automation hook in publish pipeline (SRE/Eng)
Document security & privacy implications of sampling and ensure PII filtering (Security)
Write customer-facing release notes and example migration steps for stewards (Docs)
Post-mortem and metrics review 2 weeks after rollout (PM/Analytics)
decisions: Sample rate set initially to 1% of live inference requests to balance signal and cost (decision made by Infra + PM)
Sampled-cost signature will include per-token GPU time, effective batch size distribution, observed KV cache hit rate, and normalized per-request cost metric
Profiles will require both a synthetic signature and a sampled-cost signature for Redwood-verified status — synthetic-only remains allowed but flagged as 'offline-only'
Sampled telemetry will be stored in a separate signed ledger for provenance; profile artifact will contain a signed reference and a small rollup, not raw traces
Pinning recommendations default to 'conservative' when sampled-cost delta > 10% relative to synthetic baseline; conservative means prefer older pinned version until follow-up verification completes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sampling leaks sensitive prompt content -> Mitigation: strip user content and only collect anonymized runtime metrics and aggregated histograms
Risk: additional infra cost and ingestion complexity -> Mitigation: tight retention (30d) and 1% sample cap with telemetry rollups
Risk: customers see higher cost variance causing churn -> Mitigation: show clear confidence intervals and recommended guardrails in Console
Risk: false positives in pin suggestion due to noisy short windows -> Mitigation: require minimum sample count and smoothing window (24h) before auto-suggestions
